Civil rights groups have issued travel warnings for Missouri.
Due to discriminatory policies and racial attacks in Missouri, the NAACP issued a travel warning to African Americans planning trips to Missouri.

Issued on August 28, 2017, the NAACP’s Missouri travel advisory urged all African-American U.S. travelers, tourists, and residents of Missouri to exercise extreme caution and vigilance when traveling in Missouri, following a series of suspicious racially-motivated incidents that had occurred in the state recently.

The NAACP pointed out that a recently passed Missouri law makes it harder for people to win discrimination lawsuits, and that the state’s enforcement has, to some extent, targeted minority groups, prompting the organization to issue a travel warning.
Actions violating citizens' rights are currently taking place.
“They were stopped and questioned because of their skin color, beaten, or killed,” said Rod Chester, president of the NAACP in Missouri, to The Kansas City Star.
We have received a large number of complaints, more than ever before.
This is the first such warning issued by the organization in the United States targeting a specific state.
This organization cited the Missouri University's racial slander against Black students and the death of Torrie Sanders, a 28-year-old Black male from Tennessee.
Earlier this year, Sanders died under suspicious circumstances. He ran out of fuel while traveling in Missouri and was detained by the Missouri police without charges.

People need to be prepared, whether they carry a bail bond to Missouri or let relatives know they are traveling within the state.

The travel warning is also a response to Missouri's new law, which will make it more difficult to sue companies engaging in housing or employment discrimination.

Previously, various states in the United States had passed immigration enforcement laws, requiring local law enforcement agencies to detain immigration offenders. The ACLU stated that this would increase the number of racial lawsuits and released travel advisories for Texas and Arizona.

Travel warnings are typically issued by the U.S. government targeting other countries, but recently, consulting groups have adopted this approach to address certain laws and trends within the United States.
